headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and egress allowlisted network traffic, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with a local game-playing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it is not a direct injection source. PaddleOCR can run browsers and process documents/images, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. Any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual copy-paste or external plumbing, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into godot_rl_agents prompts or configs, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem not shown in the profiles, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste bridging between outputs and prompts.
Review any browser-scraped text before reuse.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit extracted content off-host by default. godot_rl_agents has no data classes touched and no egress, but if it receives the same workspace artifacts, sensitive document content can leak through PaddleOCR's processing path. The interaction is indirect yet plausible in default document-processing setups.
conditions: IF documents or images in a shared workspace are fed to PaddleOCR, extracted content may leave the host via allowlisted egress.
IF godot_rl_agents is used to generate or store artifacts in the same workspace, those artifacts can be exposed to PaddleOCR processing.
mitigations: Separate document and game-agent workspaces.
Restrict PaddleOCR to local-only runs where possible.
Audit outbound destinations on the allowlist.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents exposes no write or network surfaces, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser execution. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, shared filesystem writes, or locking conflicts. The pair therefore has only a limited coordination risk unless an external orchestrator gives both write access to the same target.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory or database, conflicts become plausible.
IF either agent is wrapped with shared mutable state not shown in the profiles, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Serialize any handoff steps.
Check for hidden shared mounts before deployment.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images, and godot_rl_agents has no documented verification layer or downstream critique surface. If one agent's output is treated as authoritative by the other, OCR mistakes can cascade into incorrect actions or training artifacts. The pathway exists in default document-processing workflows, though the blast radius is bounded by the pair's limited scope.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is consumed by godot_rl_agents without human verification, OCR errors can propagate.
IF either agent's output is used as ground truth for downstream automation, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Add a human review step for OCR outputs.
Compare OCR results against source documents.
Reject low-confidence extractions.
Keep training data separate from operational outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated PHI, residency, or retention commitments. PaddleOCR touches documents/images and may egress to allowlisted endpoints, but there is no explicit compliance mismatch documented against godot_rl_agents. The risk is limited to undocumented deployment choices rather than a built-in violation.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated documents through PaddleOCR to a non-compliant endpoint, compliance risk increases.
IF either agent is used on data subject to residency or retention rules not represented in the profiles, a mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated documents to external OCR endpoints.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Limit logs to non-sensitive metadata.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
